core_obligations: Write the algebra as a quotient of a localisation of a polynomial algebra and reduce both cases to finite presentation over that localisation (proof lines 6017-6025).
Choose a presentation of the module over the localisation and form the intersection of the kernel with the polynomial algebra (proof lines 6026-6030).
Show the quotient by that intersection is flat over the valuation ring by torsion freeness (proof lines 6031-6034).
Conclude finite presentation over the polynomial algebra and then, by exactness of localisation, the required statement (proof lines 6035-6039).
proof_roadmap: Set up the localised polynomial presentation (proof lines 6017-6030).
Flatness of the auxiliary quotient (proof lines 6031-6034).
Finite presentation and localisation back (proof lines 6035-6039).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a valuation ring, a flat local homomorphism which is essentially of finite type is essentially of finite presentation, and that a finite module which is flat over the valuation ring is finitely presented over its algebra. The proof writes the algebra as a quotient of a localised polynomial algebra, chooses a presentation of the module over that localisation, and takes the intersection of the kernel with the polynomial algebra. That intersection localises back to the kernel, and the quotient it defines is a submodule of the module, hence flat over the valuation ring by torsion freeness, which combined with finiteness gives finite presentation over the polynomial algebra; exactness of localisation then identifies the localised submodule with the module.
